data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain by measuring transfer to a held-out task block where the checklist's items are known to be insufficient; if the panel retains accuracy above baseline on the insufficient-checklist block, it has internalized structure beyond the checklist, but if it collapses to baseline, prior accuracy was mere compliance.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the held-out block has zero structural overlap with the checklist-sufficient block, even a panel with genuine internalization will drop to baseline, making the test insensitive.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is so comprehensive that no insufficient block exists within the task domain, the evaluation cannot construct the diagnostic block at all.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the panel's reliability is genuine (i.e., the checklist helped them learn the underlying domain logic), then on a block where the checklist is insufficient, the panel should still leverage whatever structural overlap exists between the checklist-sufficient and checklist-insufficient tasks to remain above baseline. If the panel was merely following the checklist, it should perform at baseline on the insufficient block, because the checklist's mechanical application yields no signal when the items are absent or non-predictive.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
